sentences.text: Squalicorax is an extinct genus of lamniform shark, a group of sharks related to modern mako sharks, commonly called the crow shark. The name combines the Latin word for shark with the Greek word for raven.
These sharks typically measured between 1.8 and 3 meters in length, though some estimates suggest they could reach up to 5 meters, averaging around 2 meters.

Squalicorax had a body shape similar to modern gray reef sharks but possessed teeth strikingly similar to those of a tiger shark. These teeth were numerous, relatively small, curved, serrated, and up to 2.5 to 3 centimeters in height.
The largest known specimen of Squalicorax pristodontus measured up to 4.8 meters long.
Squalicorax is one of only three Cretaceous lamniform sharks known to have serrated teeth, alongside Pseudocorax and Galeocorax.
The world's largest and most complete semi-articulated Squalicorax fossil, measuring over 3 meters, was discovered in 2014 in Morden, Manitoba, Canada.
Fossil evidence shows Squalicorax was both a coastal predator and scavenger, including a tooth found embedded in the foot bone of a terrestrial hadrosaurid dinosaur.
The body shape and structure of the placoid scales indicate that Squalicorax was capable of swimming quickly.
The family Anacoracidae was established by H. Cappetta in 1987, and Squalicorax belongs to this family.
The genus Squalicorax existed from the Callovian to the Danian, spanning from 165.3 to 61.66 million years ago.
Squalicorax volgensis is the oldest species of the genus, originating from the Early Cretaceous of the Volga region and described by L. Glickman et al. in 1971.
Squalicorax pristodontus is the largest species in the genus, with estimates based on tooth size suggesting it grew to 4.8 meters in length.
It is debated whether Squalicorax actively snatched Pteranodon from the air, attacked them while diving, or simply scavenged their remains based on tooth marks found on their bones.
